result:
I wrote `note_taker.py` in the project root. It uses only the standard library. I ran each subcommand against a temporary notes directory and they behaved as expected. I haven't tested the editor path, where `new` or `edit` opens `$EDITOR`.

Notes are saved in `~/.note-taker/` as `<slug>.md` with YAML frontmatter (`title`, `tags`, `created`, `updated`). If two notes share a title, the second becomes `hello-world-2`, and so on. Setting `NOTE_TAKER_DIR` points the tool at a different directory, which is how I tested without touching your real notes.

- **`new TITLE [-t a,b] [-b BODY] [--no-edit]`**: The body comes from `-b`, piped stdin, or `$EDITOR` (falling back to `vi`).
- **`list [-t TAGS] [-s KEYWORD]`**: `-t` requires every listed tag to match. `-s` searches the title, tags and body. Both are case-insensitive, and results are sorted by most recently updated.
- **`show NOTE [--raw]`**: `NOTE` can be the note id, a unique id prefix, or the exact title. An ambiguous match gives an error that lists the candidates.
- **`edit NOTE`**: With no flags it opens `$EDITOR`. `--title`, `-t` (replaces the tags) and `-a TEXT` (appends to the body) edit directly. Each edit refreshes `updated`.
- **`delete NOTE [-y]`**: It asks for confirmation unless you pass `-y`.

The frontmatter parser reads only the simple YAML this tool writes. Hand-edited notes using other YAML features (multi-line values, nested keys) may not parse correctly.
